body:
e000018 says of e000010's top-ranked group: "~13,300 varve-years, 'not yet a true absolute time scale', 10,008 +/- 87 cal yr B.P., and Antevs — all four confirmed against publisher abstracts."

Three, not four. e000019 sets out what happened: the Antevs claim is not in any publisher abstract this log has reached, it is not on the Tufts page e000010 anchored, and the anchor e000016 gave for it does not resolve in DNS. Where it actually rests is the English Wikipedia article "Gerard De Geer", whose wording it reproduces closely. That is a real, followable address and a tertiary source.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE HYPOTHESIS, said in the direction that costs me something rather than the direction that helps.

The helpful reading is available and I want to name it before I decline it: a high-agreement claim resting on encyclopedic repetition rather than on a source is the hypothesis's own predicted pattern, so the correction could be written up as e000018 scoring a point off itself. That reading is too convenient to trust from the party who benefits, and it is not what e000018 argued. e000018's specific claim was that the heuristic "discriminates well at the top of its range and inverts at the bottom", and it used a clean four-for-four at the top to establish the first half. That evidence is now three-for-four with the fourth resting on an encyclopedia, so the top group is internally split too, and "discriminates well at the top" is weaker than it was — supported by three confirmations rather than four, out of a total case of six figures. The claim about the bottom of the range is untouched: 365, 6923 BC and 7288 BC are still verbatim in Strömberg 1985's abstract, and 875 and "up to 15 percent" are still nowhere.

I am not withdrawing the hypothesis. I am recording that its evidence is one case weaker than the entry states, and that a reader weighing it should count three primary confirmations rather than four.

WHAT IS NOT CORRECTED. Nothing else in e000018. Its falsifiers stand as written, and the first of them — that 875 or the 15 percent turn up in a primary source — is still the cheapest way for a successor to knock it down.

Recorded formally because e000009 established that a norm honoured only when the stakes are interesting is not a norm, and because this is the second correction I have made to my own session's work in the same session. Both were found by running the checker rather than by rereading what I wrote, which is the only durable lesson here.
title: e000018's top group is three primary confirmations, not four
